Module org.slb4j
Package org.slb4j.handler

Class AbstractFileHandler

java.lang.Object
org.slb4j.handler.AbstractFileHandler
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable, LayoutConfigurable, LogHandler
Direct Known Subclasses:
FileHandler, RotatingFileHandler
public abstract sealed class AbstractFileHandler extends Object implements LogHandler, AutoCloseable, LayoutConfigurable permits FileHandler, RotatingFileHandler
A log handler that writes log entries to a file. It supports log rotation triggered by file size, number of entries, or time.

    • flushLevel

      protected LogLevel flushLevel
      The minimum log level at which a flush operation is triggered.

      Defaults to LogLevel.TRACE, i.e., flushing is triggered after every log entry.

    • doHandle

      protected final void doHandle(long timestamp, String loggerName, LogLevel lvl, @Nullable String mrk, @Nullable MDC mdc, @Nullable Location loc, CharSequence msg, @Nullable Throwable t)
      Handles the processing and writing of a log entry.

      This method formats a log entry using the specified parameters, writes the formatted log entry to the associated writer, and optionally flushes the writer if the log level meets or exceeds the configured flush threshold.

      Parameters:
      timestamp - the timestamp of the log entry in milliseconds since the epoch
      loggerName - the name of the logger instance
      lvl - the log level of the entry
      mrk - an optional marker associated with the log entry, or null if not applicable
      mdc - an optional Mapping Diagnostic Context (MDC) providing contextual data for the log entry, or null if not applicable
      loc - an optional location context providing code-related metadata (e.g., class name, method name, etc.), or null if not available
      msg - the message to be logged
      t - an optional throwable associated with the log entry, such as an exception, or null if not applicable

    • checkRotation

      protected void checkRotation(long timestamp, int charsToWrite) throws IOException
      Checks whether a log rotation should occur based on the given timestamp. This method is typically overridden in subclasses to implement log rotation logic, such as file rolling based on time or size constraints. If the current implementation does not specify a rotation policy, this method may be left empty.
      Parameters:
      timestamp - the timestamp of the current log event in milliseconds since the epoch; can be used to evaluate time-based rotation criteria
      charsToWrite - the number of characters to be written to the log file in the following call
      Throws:
      IOException - if an I/O error occurs during rotation check

    • writeLayoutHeader

      protected final void writeLayoutHeader() throws IOException
      Writes the layout header to the underlying writer, if it is defined and non-empty.

      This method retrieves the header from the layout using layout.getHeader(), and writes it to the Writer instance provided by the writer() method. If the header is an empty string, no action is performed. The writer is flushed after the header is written to ensure the content is immediately written to the output.

      Throws:
      IOException - if an I/O error occurs while writing to the Writer

    • writeLayoutFooter

      protected final void writeLayoutFooter() throws IOException
      Writes the footer section of the log layout to the underlying writer, if the footer is defined and non-empty.

      This method retrieves the footer from the layout using layout.getFooter() and writes it to the Writer instance provided by the writer() method. If the footer is an empty string or the writer is null, no action is performed. After writing the footer, the writer is flushed to ensure the content is immediately written to the output destination.

      Throws:
      IOException - if an I/O error occurs while writing to or flushing the Writer

    • onShutDown

      protected final void onShutDown()
      Handles the shutdown process for the log handler, ensuring that any required cleanup tasks are performed, such as writing the footer to the log file and releasing resources.

      This method writes the footer, if available, by invoking layout.getFooter() and uses the writer() method to obtain a Writer instance. After writing the footer, the method ensures that the writer is properly closed, even in the event of an exception.

      If an IOException occurs, an error message is printed to Util.err() to indicate that the log file could not be closed successfully.

      The method is intended to be overridden in subclasses if additional custom cleanup tasks are required during shutdown.

    • shutdown

      public final void shutdown()
      Description copied from interface: LogHandler
      Initiates the shutdown process for the log handler. This method should be called to release any resources, perform cleanup tasks, and ensure finalization work for the logging system associated with this handler. Once this method is invoked, the log handler should not be expected to process any further log entries.
      Specified by:
      shutdown in interface LogHandler
